baseline_workload: Identification, diagnosis across device and account state, applicable troubleshooting, status checks, and escalation form a substantial multi-stage objective; setup actions are excluded.
probe_workload: The sufficient path has several stages: identify the customer, diagnose the device, guide any needed preliminary fix, then transfer when the locked SIM is established. On a defensible path, a missing-SIM finding leads to reseating before a subsequent check reveals the lock. Payment, line resumption and APN repair are excluded after that decisive exit; seeded setup operations are not agent work.
baseline_dependencies: Customer identification precedes support; device fixes and any bill-payment/line-resumption path require linked checks and user participation before the unresolved issue can be escalated.
probe_dependencies: Identification precedes technical support; a missing SIM may need reseating before a later SIM check exposes the decisive lock. Transfer depends on that finding and is followed by the prescribed message. No payment or other repairs are prerequisites to locked-SIM escalation.

baseline_workload: This is substantial multi-stage work for one service issue: identify the customer, diagnose overlapping device and line causes, try applicable fixes, check service, and escalate when the locked SIM remains. Setup actions are not counted as agent work.
probe_workload: Several routine stages precede the decisive locked-SIM exit: identification, device checks, guidance for airplane mode and the missing SIM as indicated, and escalation. Payment and line restoration are excluded after that exit.
baseline_dependencies: Customer identification precedes support; a suspension can be lifted only after overdue bills are paid, followed by a device reboot. Device checks and any fixes must inform whether the unresolved locked SIM warrants transfer.
probe_dependencies: Identification precedes support; a missing-SIM finding leads to reseating and a subsequent SIM check before the lock can establish escalation. No payment-to-resumption dependency is charged after that mandatory exit.

baseline_workload: One service issue requires several linked but limited stages: identify, diagnose device status, and escalate the locked SIM. Do not count every other initialized fault as a required repair before this exit.
probe_workload: Several routine stages serve one objective: identify the customer, check device status, potentially turn off observed airplane mode, diagnose the locked SIM, then transfer and notify. The locked SIM is the decisive exit; APN repair, bill payment and line resumption are excluded after its discovery.
baseline_dependencies: Identification precedes technical support, diagnostic results determine whether escalation is appropriate, and the transfer call precedes its required message. These are conditional linked stages, not an extensive handoff workflow.
probe_dependencies: Customer identification precedes technical support; device checks and any indicated airplane-mode guidance precede recognition of the locked-SIM exit, which precedes transfer and its required message. No payment or APN-repair chain is needed after that exit. Checking the SIM earlier is also defensible and would omit the airplane-mode action.

baseline_workload: One service-support objective has several stages—customer identification, device diagnosis and applicable guidance, reassessment, then escalation—but unrelated mobile-data and MMS procedures are not charged.
probe_workload: The sufficient path has several stages—identify the customer, diagnose and reseat the missing SIM, discover the lock, then transfer. APN repair and overdue-bill payment are excluded after the SIM-security exit.
baseline_dependencies: Identification precedes technical support; SIM findings govern whether reseating or escalation applies, and transfer depends on establishing that available actions cannot solve the issue. No payment or line-resumption chain is required once the locked SIM determines the exit.
probe_dependencies: Customer identification precedes support; a missing-SIM result leads to reseating and reassessment before the locked-SIM exit is established. Once established, neither billing nor APN work is a prerequisite to transfer.
